title: A Round Robin characterisation of the hydrogen sorption properties of a carbon based material
material_description: CMS 4A | Commercial microporous carbon molecular sieve, extruded cylindrical pellets ~2.2 mm diameter; the single Round Robin test material measured by all participating laboratories; apparent BET area 423(20) m2/g (N2, 77 K), DR micropore volume 0.17 cm3/g; outgassed per RRT protocol (383 K 24 h then 523 K 4 h, dynamic vacuum)
source_location: Abstract (p. 3044); Sec. 7.2.1 (p. 3050, "The maximum hydrogen adsorbed is 1.4 wt.% at 77 K and 1 MPa"); Sec. 9 Conclusions (p. 3055, "1.4(0.1) wt% at 77 K and 1 MPa")
notes: Consensus (reference) value from the four group-1 isotherms (labs 3, 6, 7, 11: static volumetric and static gravimetric), not one laboratory; measuring_lab_id is the corresponding author group because no single laboratory applies. Value (uncertainty) printed as 1.40(0.1); the meaning of the bracket is not defined. Same value in abstract, Sec. 7.2.1 and conclusions, recorded once. Measurement method coded other because it combines volumetric and gravimetric isotherms.
basis_evidence: "The adsorption of hydrogen on porous materials corresponds to an excess adsorption, which is the only experimentally accessible variable by all conventional techniques [1,3,13]." (Sec. 4.1, p. 3046). General statement; the paper does not define the basis or report two bases.
measuring_lab_id: Zlotea group, Institute for Energy, Joint Research Centre, European Commission
